historical_reviews.deepseek: Its cycle count and soft-reboot direction fit, but its credential and host-identity handling are unsafe and final-only evidence cannot establish per-cycle stability.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly separates warm OS restart from cold/AC power actions and strengthens readiness, audit and recovery requirements.
historical_reviews.history: The exact-code row-805 CPU thermal-protection record was read and excluded as a different stimulus and acceptance model.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Repeated service-interrupting reboots require confirmation and evidence per iteration; missing ordinary inputs cause conditional readiness, not a permanent block.

original_test_intent: Demonstrate that a fully populated SUT completes 25 warm OS reboots, returns to a defined ready state after each, retains every expected device and produces no disallowed BMC/system errors, hang or blue screen.
original_method: Use one owner-approved OS warm-restart mechanism on the verified host, preserve the pre-run baseline, then issue exactly 25 restarts through an authenticated session and record shutdown, boot, reconnect, service readiness, inventory and event evidence for every iteration.
manual_activity: The system owner approves the 25 service interruptions and readiness oracle; an operator keeps console/OOB recovery available and decides whether an observed anomaly permits no further restart.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/BMC/OS identity and expected fully populated device inventory
Supported warm-reboot command/API and proof it does not perform cold or AC power control
Shutdown, boot, reconnect and application/service readiness timeouts
Dedicated window, active-user/job drain and final state
Per-cycle error/device criteria, abort owner and console/OOB recovery
safety_requirements: Preserve complete BMC and OS history before any authorized clear
Do not use sshpass, disable host-key checking or log credentials
Verify no protected users, jobs or tests remain before the first restart
Never replace a warm restart with BMC power off/on, reset, AC cut or forced action
Stop on boot/reconnect timeout, hang, blue screen, device loss, persistent event, unexpected power transition or incomplete evidence
Do not automatically retry a failed cycle
Restore the owner-approved final workload and connectivity state
agent_execution_scope: Validate host/BMC identity, trusted authentication, inventory and restart method
Archive the baseline and initialize an exactly 25-entry ledger
Issue only the approved warm OS restart after approval
For every iteration, detect shutdown, boot identity, network/session return, service readiness, inventory and complete BMC/OS events
Stop and preserve evidence on the first failed readiness gate
Summarize results without issuing PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED
engineer_actions: Approve the warm-restart method, window, readiness and abort rules
Drain or accept impact to workloads and users
Maintain recovery console/OOB access and supervise anomalies
Review each cycle and own the final verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A 25-iteration OS reboot loop targets the intended stimulus, but the shown sshpass and disabled-host-key wrapper can leak credentials or hit the wrong host; a final SEL tail also misses intermediate events and device state.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Invoke the platform-approved warm OS restart through a trusted authenticated session, then require the same verified host identity, readiness and complete evidence checkpoint before incrementing the cycle ledger.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Exactly 25 warm reboots, full CPU/DIMM/HDD/GPU/network population, 30/180-minute estimates and all source criteria remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the target and warm-restart primitive, preserve baseline, serialize 25 restart/readiness checkpoints, stop on the first anomaly and perform a complete final-state comparison.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds trusted session identity, workload drain, objective readiness milestones, complete cycle-local evidence and console recovery while preserving OS-level warm reboot coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Cold power, AC cycling or merely observing the final boot does not cover 25 verified warm OS restart transitions.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Frequent restarts disrupt users and can expose storage replay, driver initialization, firmware handoff or intermittent enumeration faults.

project_override_considerations: The Project must name what `warm` means on this OS and platform. If the selected API performs a hardware reset or power transition, that difference is uncovered or separately reviewed rather than silently accepted as equivalent.
expected_evidence: Verified target/OS/BMC identity, trusted restart method, inventory, approval and workload-drain record
Immutable pre-clear BMC/OS/device/sensor baseline and authorized clear audit if used
Cycles 1-25 ledger with request, shutdown, boot identity, reconnect and service-ready timestamps
Complete per-cycle BMC/OS events, device inventory and exit/status data
Any timeout, hang, blue screen, device loss, unexpected power transition, error or missing-evidence record
Final state and inventory comparison, session/security audit, recovery actions and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Row 1527's Items, reboot procedure and stability criteria consistently define repeated warm recovery. The generic word `Reboot` needs a Project-approved OS method, but the adjacent cold-reboot row and duplicate thermal row clarify rather than contradict this row's identity.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Warm-restart command, readiness timeouts, authentication and recovery are finite inputs. The test purpose and acceptance direction are clear enough for conditional execution.

review_improvement: Replaces an insecure, weakly evidenced SSH loop with an identity-bound 25-cycle warm-restart contract that preserves the exact disruption and produces evidence for every recovery claim.
independent_technical_reasoning: A warm-reboot test is primarily a repeated state-transition and re-enumeration test, not a count of accepted reboot commands. Each iteration must prove that the same host reached the agreed application-ready state with the complete hardware set; otherwise subsequent iterations conceal the first failure rather than add coverage.
